summary: Maven Solutions comments on the E-7 show cause order, scoring PJM's large-load tariff posture Conditional under its own Civic Bankability Rating Standard and recommending tariff revisions for each of the five reform categories.
ask: Require PJM to file tariff revisions or a detailed evidentiary showing on all five reform categories, including time-bounded study commitments, a large-load cost-causation method and a flexible large-load tariff class.

points.point: Maven rates PJM's posture Conditional with two keystone flags, Ratepayer Protection and Financial Surety, which it says warrant Commission intervention.
points.quote: PJM's current tariff posture on large-load interconnection scores CONDITIONAL under the Civic Bankability Rating Standard with two active keystone flags

points.point: Maven cites the 2027/28 auction as the first to miss the reliability requirement, 6,516.6 MW UCAP short at a 14.4% reserve margin.
points.quote: which PJM reported as 6,516.6 MW UCAP below the RTO Reliability Requirement.

points.point: Maven says large-load study processes lack a bounded time-to-service commitment or public reporting of completion times.
points.quote: proceed without a bounded time-to-service commitment, without public reporting on median or 90th-percentile completion timelines, and without a customer-facing remedy mechanism for delayed studies.

points.point: Recommendation 2 asks that upgrade and capacity costs caused by large loads go to the responsible load class, with per-upgrade disclosure.
points.quote: attributes transmission upgrade costs and capacity procurement costs caused by large-load interconnection to the responsible load class, not to Load Serving Entities or residential rate classes

points.point: Recommendation 4 asks for flexible large-load tariff classes with defined compensation, reliability crediting and financial surety.
points.quote: provide for curtailable or interruptible service with defined compensation; (ii) include contribution-to-reliability crediting

points.point: Maven says this is one of six coordinated comments across dockets EL26-67 through EL26-72.
points.quote: These Comments are one of six substantive Comments Maven files this cycle across the six Show Cause dockets initiated on June 18, 2026 (EL26-67 through EL26-72).

throughLine.text: Comments on the E-7 show cause order in EL26-67 that map Maven's recommendations to the order's five reform categories: study process, cost shifting, co-location, flexible load service and proximate generation.
